newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Labour sees end November as crunch time.
newsitem.headline: NZ Labour sees end November as crunch time.

text.p: New Zealand First and the main opposition Labour party wrapped up their seventh round of talks on Thursday with Labour leader Helen Clark pointing to the end of November as crunch time for the talks.
"If a government's to be in place for the new parliament then probably the last week of November looks interesting," Clark told journalists at the end of the hour and a half meeting.
Parliament must meet no later than December 10.

NZ First holds the balance of power after the October 12 election and is negotiating separately with Labour and the caretaker conservative National government, led by Jim Bolger, over the shape of the next administration.
If parliament met before a deal was struck Clark said the matter would go to a vote of confidence.
"There will be two people seeking a vote of confidence. One will be me, the other will be Mr Bolger."
She said if she won a vote of confidence under that scenario she would lead a minority government.
Asked what would happen if neither Labour nor National won a vote of confidence, Clark said: "I think someone would win.
"I think the talks are going very well. From our point of view we are happy," Clark said.
The parties have scheduled informal talks for Friday and further formal sessions on Tuesday.
